annotations.title: Territorial Integrity of Ukraine : resolution / adopted by the General Assembly | Refworld

content.text:
**Under international law and by the position of most countries, Crimea belongs to Ukraine, not Russia.** Russia has controlled and occupied Crimea since 2014, after annexing it, but that annexation is widely considered illegal and is not internationally recognized by the UN General Assembly, the United States, the EU, Ukraine, and many other states.

In 2014, the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 68/262 affirming Ukraine’s territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and declaring the Crimea referendum invalid. ([refworld.org](https://www.refworld.org/legal/resolution/unga/2014/98780?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is:

- **De jure / legally:** Crimea is part of **Ukraine**.
- **De facto / in practical control:** Crimea is controlled by **Russia**.
- **Russia’s position:** Crimea is part of Russia.
- **Most of the international community’s position:** Crimea is **Ukrainian territory under Russian occupation**.
